prompt:
Implement the unfinished `vcf_logs` package as a Python standard-library-only client for the supplied VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 Operations for Logs contract.

`VCFLogsClient(base_url, username, password, provider="Local")` must authenticate once with `POST /api/v2/sessions`, then `list_events(*, since_timestamp, page_size=100, timeout=None, view=None, content_pack_fields=None)` must retrieve every event newer than `since_timestamp` through `GET /api/v2/events/{+path}`. Page forward in ascending timestamp order: request `timestamp/GT <cursor>` with `limit` and `order-by-direction=ASC`, advance the cursor to the last timestamp from each full page, and stop only after a short page. Reject an incomplete response (`complete` is false) instead of emitting partial data. Return the complete collection in stable `(timestamp, text)` order.

Send the session ID as `Authorization: Bearer <sessionId>`. Encode the timestamp constraint as a reserved path expansion with its space percent-encoded. Optional `timeout`, `view`, and repeated `content-pack-fields` query fields must be included when set and omitted entirely when unset or empty; never send them as empty values. Use JSON request/response bodies with the appropriate `Accept` and `Content-Type` headers.

Complete the module CLI so `python -m vcf_logs --base-url URL --username USER --password PASSWORD --provider PROVIDER --since TIMESTAMP --page-size SIZE` performs the same complete retrieval and writes one compact, key-sorted JSON object per line in the same stable order. The supplied loopback mock is the only endpoint used by verification. Run `python3 tests/verify.py` to check the implementation.
